Commentary.Commentary: Okay. After a 1-5 drubbing at the hands of India at home, South Africa badly needed this series win to raise their spirits. Remove the previous series and the one to England in England and you will find that they have actually won 9 out of their last 11 bilateral ODI series including this one, which is their second consecutive series win in the Island Nation. Now, their next aim will be a 5-0 whitewash. Can Sri Lanka avoid that? They have lost their 5th ODI series on the trot, winning just 1 out of their last 18 games. Not to mention that this is also their 10th straight loss in ODIs at home. Save aside that win against India in Dharamsala in 2017, they have struggled big time with the white ball. Join us on Wednesday, 8th August, 2018, at 1430 local (0900 GMT) for the 4th ODI at this very ground. ADIOS! TAKE CARE!

Victorious South African captain, Faf du Plessis, says that it was a brilliant display of cricket by his side. First praises the batting, especially the debutant Reeza Hendricks. Then says that it is amazing to see one or two guys put their hands up in almost every game. On the high-scoring match, Faf says that he did enjoy the batsmen scoring runs, even against his team's bowling, as it was a good test for his side. He also says that he enjoyed his bowlers going for wickets in spite of the runs being scored. On his own injury, he informs that he will assess tomorrow and then check how his 'young' shoulder responds in the morning.

Sri Lankan skipper, Angelo Mathews, admits that it was disappointing the way Sri Lanka started with the ball, but is happy for the fact that they pulled it back in the middle overs. However, he rues the way the death overs panned out, adding that 364 was too much to chase on this wicket. Praises Hendricks, Duminy and Miller and stresses that the Lankan team is developing, on how to play different phases in One-Day cricket.

Reeza Hendricks is the Man of The Match for his scintillating century. Hendricks says that he already had a taste of international cricket having played T20Is but is elated to have done well in the One-Day format. Stresses that with such a good side, it is very difficult to break in and is happy to have done well. On the surface, he says that he enjoyed batting on it as it was very true. On being asked about recording the fastest century by a debutant in ODIs, Reeza smiles and says that he was not aware of any such record.

Lungi Ngidi is having a chat with Shaun Pollock. He says that the Proteas were aware that it was a good pitch given the score their batsmen had put up but what they did not expect was the ball not moving much and the track being absolutely flat. Adds that they still felt it resembled a true South African wicket, where you get value for your shots. Admits that the plan was always to try and pick up wickets and not be defensive. Is smiling on being asked about the series win, especially after the drubbing in the Tests. On the collision with de Kock, Ngidi laughs and says that he felt that he ran into a brick wall. Will go back to the dressing room and check the replays, he adds, to see what happened exactly. Now for the presentation.

Earlier, Angelo Mathews won the toss and decided to do something different - chase. However, a half century from Hashim Amla, followed by a century from Reeza Hendricks on debut and then some late blows from JP Duminy and David Miller took the score to 363. Thisara Perera picked up 4 wickets but went for plenty in the second half of his spell as the Proteas hammered 71 in the last 5 overs.

Even though they had a big score behind their backs, the bowlers aimed to take wickets and bowl the opposition out. Lungi Ngidi was impressive again and finished with 4 wickets while Andile Phehlukwayo surprisingly picked up 3 again, this time on an unresponsive deck. Quinton de Kock rotated his bowlers quite effectively in Faf du Plessis' absence, with only Tabraiz Shamsi finishing his quota of 10 overs.

The two Dananjayas got together - one with an 'H' and the other without 'H'. They played normal cricket, showing the top order how good a pitch this was. Managed to add 95 and give some respectability to the score. Dhananjaya de Silva was unlucky to miss out on a deserving ton and perhaps we might have had a closer game if the hosts had managed to string more partnerships.

With the target as steep as 364, it was no surprise that the Lankans came out all guns blazing. Even with the ball not doing much, the home side kept losing its batsmen one by one. At 155/6, needing more than 200, it seemed like we would be back home earlier than usual. But it was not to be.

So the series is sealed with 2 matches to go. South Africa have won 3 games on the trot in this series and 11 in succession against Sri Lanka. The only positive for the Lankans was that there was some fight offered by Akila Dananjaya and Dhananjaya de Silva, reducing the defeat margin to under 100.

OUT! Caught and bowled! Match and series win for South Africa. A short ball outside off, Lakmal looks to pull but gets a massive top edge which goes straight up in the air. Two people go for the catch - the bowler and the keeper. Neither look at each other nor communicate. Both get ready to take it. Almost collide into each other. But because Ngidi is taller, he takes it with his palms skywards, way over de Kock's face, leaving the stand-in captain smiling. SOUTH AFRICA WIN BY 78 RUNS!
A short ball on middle, slogged towards mid on.
Goes right back in his crease and blocks. Shamsi finishes his 10-over quota - the first to do so in this run chase - 10-0-62-2.
Outside off, a push and a miss.
FOUR! Great shot! Tossed up outside off, Kumara gets down and slogs it over mid on for a boundary!
The batsman plays the pull shot. One run added to the total.
Full and outside off, chipped over mid off for a run.
Okay.... so Shamsi becomes the first bowler in this inning to bowl his 10th over. Will he complete it?
Dropped short, heaved towards mid-wicket for a single.
A long hop, pulled wide of mid on for a couple. Good fielding by the fielder running from the circle, getting to the ball and then dragging it back in.
Full and straight, defended back to the bowler.
The batsman appears to have been struck on the thigh pad.
Stays back in his crease and defends.
A bouncer, Kumara ducks.

Meanwhile, a bit of a positive news for Sri Lanka. They are losing this series here to the Proteas but the Colts have just managed to eke out a 7-run win over India in the third Youth ODI at the SSC, Colombo. The team successfully defended a 'modest' score of 220. After losing both the Tests by an innings and then the first ODI, the Under-19 team has bounced back well to win two on the trot. Positive signs for the future?
A short ball, pulled through mid-wicket for a single.
This one goes straight, does not spin at all, Lahiru works it towards square leg.
Another forward defense.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full and around off, spinning away, Kumara comes forward to defend but the ball spins past the outside edge.
Lahiru Kumara is the last man in.

OUT! BOWLED! South Africa are a wicket away from a series win. Floated outside off, Jayasuriya looks to flick but the ball spins in, going right through the gap between bat and pad. Then hits the timber behind. Second wicket for Shamsi.
WIDE. The ball is down the leg side but the batsman still goes after it. Wide signalled by the umpire.
Outside off, punched wide of mid on for a single.
A low full toss, pushed straight to short mid-wicket.
Prabath Jayasuriya is the new man in at number 10.

OUT! There is a feather and de Silva has to go! No century for him, which was the only interesting part in this dead run chase. Phehlukwayo has his third. A short ball outside off, Dhananjaya looks to pull but misses. There seems to be a deviation and a noise as the Proteas appeal for the catch but umpire Nigel Llong has not heard anything. Not surprising. The crowd is making way too much noise. Captain de Kock is confident and wants a review and the first replay seems to indicate an edge. Snickometer confirms it as well. The decision is reversed and the batsman has to go. Russel Arnold informs us on air that DdS was walking towards the dressing room once he hit it but then stopped when Llong did not raise his finger. Fine enterprising innings. If only he had partners...
Boy, we have a review now. Has de Silva under-edged this one to the keeper?
Mid off goes down, while fine leg comes up.
SIX! Second of the over! This is now de Silva's highest ODI score. Some stylish way of getting there too. Backs away to the leg side and then slaps the length ball over cover. Goes all the way.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
SIX! Fine shot. A short ball, around off, de Silva pulls it over mid-wicket and clears the ropes with ease! 97 more needed from 52 balls now. He equals his previous highest score in ODIs.
A short ball outside off, Lakmal pulls it, not with too much control, through square leg for a single.
Full on middle, pushed down to long on for a single.
Full and straight, SL looks to defend but gets a thick inside edge onto his pads.
Full and around off, watchfully pushed back.

LBW appeal, turned down. Full and around middle, spinning down, Suranga looks to defend but misses and is hit on the pads. Shamsi appeals and nearly falls down while doing so, but the umpire is not interested. De Kock is not interested in the review. Looked to be sliding down the leg side...
WIDE. Similar ball, Lakmal looks to flick but misses.
A touch short, whipped past leg gully for a couple.
Floated on middle, de Silva comes down the track and pushes it towards long on for a single.
POWERPLAY 3! The match has lasted this far. 5 fielders allowed outside the 30-yard circle now. Here comes Tabraiz Shamsi. 7-0-48-1 so far.
Ouch! Another short ball, Suranga looks to pull but misses and is hit on the body.
Fuller length up, pushed towards long on but short mid-wicket intercepts.
FOUR! A short one first up to Lakmal, outside off, he swings hard but gets a top edge which flies over the keeper to the fence behind. 109 more needed from 62 balls.
Full and outside off, driven towards long off for a single.
Suranga Lakmal is the new man in.

OUT! The 95-run stand is broken. Finally a wicket for South Africa. A short ball outside off, Akila Dananjaya looks to pull but only gets a top edge. The ball goes only as far as mid off where Lungi Ngidi makes no mistake. Akila walks off but not before injecting some life in this chase. They might be going down but at least not too badly.
A length ball outside off, de Silva punches it down the ground for a single. 250 UP FOR SRI LANKA! Did not think they will get this far. 114 more needed from 65 balls.
Slowly tossed up outside off, Akila backs away and looks to cut but misses.
Comes down the track but is then yorked by Duminy. Pushes it to the off side.
Very full, around off, swept behind square on the leg side for a single.
Outside off, this is steered behind point for a couple.
FOUR! Nicely done. A tad short outside off, de Silva backs away and punches it through the covers for a boundary! 118 more needed from 70 balls. The stand is now worth 91 from 71 balls!
Outside off, reverse swept straight to short third man.
FOUR! SPANKED! Another slower ball, outside off, Dananjaya picks the change in pace and swipes it over mid-wicket for a boundary!
Full and around off, heaved straight to short mid-wicket.
Comes down the track and pulls it towards mid-wicket for a single.
A short ball, slower in pace, Dhananjaya looks to pull but misses and is hit on the pads.
Outside off, a slash and a miss.
Third man goes back now. Fine leg comes up as a result.

FOUR! Smart batting. A little bit of pace on that, slightly short outside off, a bit of room and Dhananjaya just steers it past short third man for a boundary. The stand is now worth 82 from 64 balls. 127 more needed from 77 balls.
WIDE. A slower delivery gone awry, short and down the leg side, de Silva cannot connect with his pull.
Very full, driven straight to the bowler.
Short and outside off, chopped towards deep point for a couple.
FOUR! Not a bad shot. Tossed up outside off, Dananjaya jumps down the track, stays leg side of the ball and lofts it inside out over cover. Moves to 31 from 35 balls with his third boundary.
Full again, driven straight to that man at silly mid off.
JUST SHORT! Full and outside off, Dananjaya chips it uppishly towards the silly mid off fielder. He dives in front but the ball does not carry.
Around off, watchfully defended.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. They manage to come back for the second.
Another back foot punch, just a single.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.

Excellent stop by Quinton de Kock. On a length outside off, Dhananjaya guides it through the vacant first slip region. That is a very good shot as third man was inside the circle. However, superman de Kock flies to his right and makes a half-stop, parrying the ball towards point. Just a single.
Dropped short, pulled straight to short mid-wicket.
FOUR! Finds the gap. A length ball outside off, de Silva chops it past backward point and gets a boundary.
Andile Phehlukwayo is back. 5-0-37-1 so far.

Comes down the track and pushes it towards long off for a single. 4th ODI fifty for Dhananjaya. Forget the game, forget the run chase, this guy has played well. At least someone has had the gumption to fight. Well played. Can he get to a century now?
On middle and leg, flicked away for a run.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket. One run added to the total.
Outside off, punched off the back foot for a run.
Driven towards the mid on region.
Short and outside off, punched towards cover where Tabraiz Shamsi misfields and concedes a couple.
The batsman does well to stand tall and play that short delivery. They pick up a single.
WIDE. Bouncer! The batsman ducks in time to let that one go over him. The umpire signals a wide.
A short ball outside off, Akila looks to play the upper cut but misses.
The batsman plays the pull shot. The batsmen have run through for a single.

SIX! Off the top edge. Some luck for Sri Lanka, albeit too late in the innings. A short ball outside off, de Silva looks to hook but the bounce gets big on him. He goes through with his shot, with his eyes closed and when he opens them, sees the ball cross the ropes over backward square leg. Also raises the 50-run stand.
A short ball outside off, de Silva looks to defend but the ball rises sharply and he fends it down to the off side.
On a length outside off, dabbed to third man for a single.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Full and around off, watchfully blocked out.
The batsman plays a sweep shot. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Full and outside off, driven through mid off for one. 200 UP FOR SRI LANKA. Another 164 needed from just 105 balls.
Dropped short, pulled away for a run.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot. They pick up a single.

DRINKS BREAK. Another of those you-will-not-miss-much-even-if-you-sleep-for-a-day matches. The South African score is way too much for the Lankans and the home side is not even able to offer a fight. So much so, that the 7th wicket stand could register the first 50-partnership of the innings. Anyways, finally, JP Duminy is given the ball.
Very full outside off, pushed towards cover for a run.
A bit of extra pace, short outside off, Akila looks to play the upper cut but misses.
On a length around off, angled in, Dananjaya looks to tuck it to the leg side but the ball comes on slowly and he nearly spoons a return catch. Goes just wide of the bowler towards mid on.
Full and straight, driven towards mid off.
Fuller this time, pushed towards third man again, for another run.
On a length outside off, steered towards third man for a single. The stand is now worth 40 from 28 balls. 169 more needed from 113 balls.
Quinton de Kock going for the kill. Kagiso Rabada is back. 6-0-21-0 so far.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot. One run added to the total.
The batsman works it down the leg side. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Down the leg side, Dds misses out, flicking it straight to short fine leg.
FOUR! A hat-trick! Too full again, de Silva does an action replay of the previous delivery, only this time, the sweep is through square leg. 6th boundary in the last 14 balls!

FOUR! SMOKED! Floated, around off, de Silva gets down and sweeps this powerfully through mid-wicket for a boundary again! 176 more needed from 118 balls. Dhananjaya moves to 33 from 36 balls with his 4th boundary. The stand is worth 33 too, from 23 deliveries.

FOUR! Innovation from de Silva. Full and outside off, Dhananjaya brings out the reverse sweep but is not quite fluent with the execution. Gets a bit of a bottom edge but it is good enough to go past the keeper to the third man fence.
The batsman works it down the leg side. The batsmen have picked up a couple of runs.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.

FOUR! A length ball again, angling away, Dananjaya minus the 'H' goes inside out over cover and gets a boundary. Moves to 12 from 10 balls with his second four. The stand moves to 23 from 19 balls. 186 more needed to win from 122 balls.
On a length and straight, watchfully defended.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. They pick up a single.

A short ball, around middle, angled in, de Silva pulls it towards deep square leg. Andile Phehlukwayo nearly makes a meal of it as the ball goes off his hand towards the ropes but he recovers well to keep the batsmen to a couple.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single. 10 runs from the over, another rarity in this innings.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman.

FOUR! The Dhananjaya with an 'H' hits this hard now. Floated outside off, de Silva gets down on one knee and smashes it over cover for a boundary. Second of the over - a rarity seeing two balls cross the rope in the same 6-ball spell for the Lankans with the bat.
Full and outside off, driven towards long off for a single.
FOUR! That is a bad ball, a long hop, Dananjaya pulls it through mid-wicket for a boundary. Less than 200 needed... if that can serve as an inspiration for the Lankans...
Tossed up around middle, pushed towards short mid-wicket.
Threads this through the covers and gets a couple. Good sliding stop by the fielder in the deep...
On a length outside off, watchfully played from the crease.
Outside off, played towards point for a single.
Around off, tucked through mid-wicket for a run.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full and outside off, driven through the covers for a single.
Full and outside off, driven through mid off for a single. Just a run and a wicket from that over - Shamsi's figures read 5-0-24-1.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full and around leg, flicked towards square leg.
Who is next? Akila Dananjaya it is...

OUT! The decision stays as it is as umpire's call comes into play. The review is retained by Sri Lanka but they are being detained by South Africa. Full and around middle, Mathews gets down to sweep but it is too full to be employing the broom. He misses and is hit on the pads. Shamsi appeals vociferously and eventually, the umpire gives in. Angelo initially starts to walk but then Dhananjaya calls him back, reminding him of the DRS. Unfortunately, that cannot help him or his side much as Hawk Eye shows the ball to be clipping the leg stump, which means he has to go.
Mathews has been given out LBW! He starts to walk back but is then reminded by de Silva that the review is available...
A touch short, worked straight to short mid-wicket.
Full and around middle, defended watchfully.
Straight again, pushed towards mid on.
A bit too straight, clipped through square leg for a couple. 209 more needed from 145 balls. The stand is worth 31 from 38 balls.
WIDE. Down the leg side, no trouble at all for the batsman.
Full and outside off, Angelo works it through mid-wicket for a run.
A short ball around off, Mathews swivels and pulls it towards backward square leg for a single.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman.
Full on middle, pushed towards mid on.
Willem Mulder is back on. 3-0-15-1 so far.

On middle and leg, clipped through square leg for a single. For the second over in a row, Sri Lanka have scored 5 runs in the first half of the over and then only 1 in the next half. Beats the purpose of that early boundary. Meanwhile, 150 is up for Sri Lanka at the halfway mark, though they are still some distance away from the halfway score.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
Tucks it straight to square leg.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Full and outside off, swept through mid-wicket for a single.

FOUR! 'Probably Mathews has realized that the best way to play Shamsi is to not allow him to pitch the ball', says Russel Arnold on air. Tossed up outside off, Mathews comes down the track and pummels it down the ground through mid off for a boundary. 216 more needed from 155 balls. Mathews moves to 30 from 37 balls with his third four.
Down the leg side, helped through fine leg for a single. So after scoring 5 runs from the first 3 balls, only a single is scored in the next 3.
Outside off, punched straight to mid off.
A yorker outside off, Mathews backs away, looking to go inside out but only gets it back to the bowler.
Now he calmly steers it to third man for a single. Moves to 10 from 16 balls.
FOUR! Biffed away. A length ball outside off, de Silva gets sideways a touch to the leg side and blasts it wide of mid off. The fielder puts in a slide to his left but in vain.
On a length outside off, de Silva rises with the bounce and pushes it towards point.
FOUR! SMASH! A full toss outside off, Mathews clobbers this over mid-wicket and gets a boundary. 226 more needed from 162 balls.

Ahh... wood prevents a wicket. Floated outside off, spins back in sharply, Mathews walks across to flick but misses. Is hit right in front of the stumps and the Proteas start to appeal for the LBW, before realizing the inside edge.
Full and outside off, worked through mid-wicket for a single to take the partnership to 10 from 19 balls.
The batsman works it down the leg side.
On middle and leg, flicked away, straight to short mid-wicket.

Short and outside off, Mathews goes back and cuts it through point. Ngidi, who just finished the previous over, has enough gas to run to his right from short third man to dive and stop it with his right hand. Superb commitment. Just a single.
Now he gets the pull shot away and earns a single.
He had the license to kill but missed out. Short and outside off, a flash and a miss.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
Full and outside off, a floated a bit, Angelo drives it towards cover.
Banged in short, Mathews slips and pulls it through mid-wicket for a single.
On a length around off, watchfully defended.
Short and outside off, cut through cover and point for a single.
A leg slip comes in. Quinton de Kock, who is the active captain, is shuffling his players around.
Full and outside off, driven towards mid off.
Full and around off, pushed back to the bowler.
The batsman has played it fine down the leg side. The batsmen have picked up a couple of runs.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Full and outside off, Mathews leans and drills a cover drive wide of long off for a single.
On a length outside off, watchfully defended. Sri Lanka are still 6 runs ahead of South Africa at this stage... but have lost wayyyy too many wickets. The Proteas were 120/2.
Outside off, left alone.
ANOTHER WIDE. One more is slipped down the leg side, Dhananjaya tries the pull but misses out.
Full and outside off, de Silva pushes at it but gets a thick outside edge. However, it does not carry to the keeper behind.
WIDE. Slips this down the leg side, de Silva misses his flick.
Dhananjaya de Silva is the new man in. Possibly the last ray of hope for the Lankans.

OUT! Half the side back in the hut. The elusive 50-run stand seems to be far away. A short ball, around middle, Mendis looks to pull but is done in by the extra bounce. Mistimes his pull and it goes towards deep square leg. Willem Mulder gets across to his right, goes low and takes a fantastic catch because the ball was dipping in. Nearly drops it but holds on. Third wicket for Lungi Ngidi and he will be happy, even though he has gone for runs. Sri Lanka, well, need 240 more from 183 balls to keep the series alive.
On a length and straight, watchfully defended.

FOUR! Nice work done by the physio. Seems to have energized Mendis. A short ball outside off, Mendis stands back and pulls it with aplomb over mid-wicket for a boundary. The stand is worth 43 from 46 balls while Mendis moves to 31 from 32 balls with his 4th four.

A bit of a delay with this already-snoozing over-rate. One of the batsmen is down - is it Mendis? Seems to be struggling with cramps. The physio is out in the middle. Meanwhile, the crowd is finally realizing that enjoying the music is perhaps not a bad option as opposed to the cricket...
Full and around off, spinning in, watchfully defended.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket.
Full on middle, Kusal leans and flicks it uppishly, just wide of short mid-wicket, for a single to long on.

FOUR! STUPENDOUS! Mendis is usually strong in the mid-wicket region and Shamsi gives him the perfect ball to exploit that area. Tossed up ball, outside off, spinning in, Kusal gets down and mows the slog sweep with the spin, over mid-wicket, wide of the man in the deep.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
On middle and leg, quietly worked through square leg for a single.
Spin time. Tabraiz Shamsi to bowl.
The batsman plays the pull shot. They pick up a single.
A short ball outside off, Mendis looks to play the upper cut but is beaten due to the extra bounce.
A short ball now, Mathews looks to pull but miscues it off the top edge towards deep square leg. A single taken.
Action replay of the previous delivery.
On a length outside off, punched straight to cover.
The cutter outside off, Mathews looks to punch it through the off side but is a tad early into the shot. Gets it off the inside edge towards mid on.
A short ball outside off, Kusal tries playing a ferocious pull shot but the bounce is a bit high for him. The ball goes only as far as short mid-wicket.
Too straight, Angelo clips it through mid-wicket for one. The stand is now worth 30 from 32 balls.
Waits for this one to come to him and steers it to third man for a run. Moves to 20 from 25 balls.
FOUR! Timing. This is on a length outside off, Mendis gives himself some room to the leg side and thumps it wide of mid off for a boundary.
Full and outside off, hit straight to cover.
Full on middle, bunted down the ground to long on for a single. 259 more needed from 203 balls...
Outside off, punched behind point for a couple.

Full on middle and leg, flicked straight to mid on. Mendis wants the single but his captain is not interested. Lungi Ngidi keeps charging in from short mid-wicket but then slips while trying to return the ball. Mendis is still hopeful of increasing his run tally but Mathews firmly says no.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.
Outside off, Mathews is squared up in defense and the ball goes off the outside edge through the vacant second slip area towards third man. A run taken.
Outside off, punched straight to mid off.

Nearly a wicket after the break! Full and outside off, Mendis looks to drive but the ball sticks off the surface a bit. Spoons off the bat face and rolls wide of cover towards mid off. A short extra cover would have gobbled it. A single taken. The stand moves to 20 from 21 balls.

Drinks break. Sri Lanka need Rohit Sharma's highest individual score in ODIs off 210 balls to win this game. But sadly, they don't have a batsman of that caliber. Can Mathews or Kusal do it? South Africa must be commended for their bowling. Lungi Ngidi once again impressed with the new ball and then both the all-rounders have picked one each.
Straighter delivery, played out towards mid-wicket to end the over. 11 from this over.

FOUR! The Sri Lankan skipper won't go down without a fight. A wayward short delivery by Andile and it has been given some direction by Mathews. He just helps it across with the pull shot and finds the boundary at fine leg. 100 up for Sri Lanka.

SIX! Gone all the way! Good length ball angling into the batsman around off, Mathews uses his feet again and goes through with his lofted shot. Finds the sweet spot of his bat and it flies all the way over the bowler's head.
Wide! Loses his radar and slips a length ball down the leg side. Mathews leaves it.
Serves a length ball on the pads, Mathews even fails to put it away. Only manages to push it towards mid-wicket.
Good length ball on off, Angelo punches from the back foot but once again not in the gap.
It would have been a half-volley on the pads for Mathews. But in an attempt to use his feet, the Sri Lankan skipper yorks himself. Can't do much after that as he digs it out towards mid off.
Slower one, landing full and around off, Mendis mistimes his drive towards mid on.
This one is on the pads, it's helped to fine leg for one.
Mathews plays it with an angled bat and guides it to third man. One run added to the total.
In line of the stumps, Mendis covers the line and pushes it back.

Good stop! A length ball outside off, Mathews makes room and slaps it through the line. Debutant Hendricks dives across to his right at extra cover and makes a half stop. He parries it towards mid off. Duminy who in anticipation has run to his left from mid off has to turn full 360 degrees to get to the ball. Picks it up and sends it back in play. A single taken. Three saved, I should say by Reeza.
Tries finding the blockhole but ends up bowling a low full toss, Mathews digs it out towards mid on.
Knocks a full ball down through mid on for a single.
On a length around off, Angelo sticks back to punch it out towards covers. Not in the gap. Going nowhere with the chase at the moment, Sri Lanka.
The batsman works it down the leg side. One run added to the total.
Short in length and outside off, Mendis stays back and cuts it through point for a couple of runs.
A length ball around off, defended off the front foot.
Mendis has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Wide! Sliding down the leg side, Mendis tries flicking but misses.
Full and outside off, driven wide of mid off. Dot ball to end a successful over.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball to covers.
Full and on middle, Mathews stays back and pushes it towards mid-wicket.
Skipper Angelo Mathews walks in next with Sri Lanka staring down the barrel.

OUT! There is bat! Quinton is right. Mulder is all smiles. Perera is walking. Sri Lanka in all sorts of trouble. For a striker like Thisara, this is a tame dismissal. Attempting an innocuous flick off his pads and getting a faint tickle behind. The umpire initially shows no interest in the appeal and on the insistence of de Kock, they go for the referral. The Snicko shows deflection and that's all the third umpire needs to overturn the on-field call. The move to send Thisara up the order flops.
Appeal for a catch. Not given. Quinton de Kock is very sure and hence South Africa take the DRS. Inside edge or pads? There was some sound.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They manage to come back for the second.
Sliding down the leg side, Mendis tucks it off his pads wide of mid on and crosses.
Full and around off, it's lofted over mid off and the fielder from the ring runs after it. The ball drops and then spins back and Duminy collects it easily. A couple of runs taken.
The batsman picked that bouncer early and let it through to the keeper.
On a length and outside off, punched from the back foot to covers.
Another back foot defense by Thisara. Surely, he is not sent up to do that.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
A length ball on middle, helped down to long leg for a couple.
Wide! Bowls it wide outside off, Perera throws his bat at it but fails to connect.
Powerplay 2 time. Maximum of 4 fielders are now allowed outside the ring till the 40th over, if the chase lasts till then.
Outside off, left alone. 73/3 in the Powerplay, a good run-rate but they have lost one wicket too many.
Physio comes out. Faf du Plessis has hurt his shoulder and is going off the field to receive some medical attention. South Africa will hope their skipper is fine. Junior Dala is the substitute.

DROPPED! But what an effort! Give credit to Faf for reaching there. Many would not have even got any hand on it. Mulder delivers a short ball outside off, Perera stands back to pull it across the line but gets a massive top edge. It balloons in the air, du Plessis from inside the ring at mid-wicket runs back and then puts in a full length dive to attempt the catch. However, he fails to hold onto it. Would have been a stunner. Duminy who came in from the deep picks the ball and sends it back in play. Meanwhile, Faf is down flat on the ground, holding his shoulder.
FOUR! Shot! An overpitched ball around off, Thisara gets forward and drills his drive down the ground for a powerful boundary.
Width on offer outside off, Perera flashes his blade through the line but gets a bottom edge behind. De Kock collects it on one bounce.
FOUR! On the pads, Thisara nudges it fine down the leg side for a boundary.
Good length ball on middle, defended off the back foot.
Willem Mulder to bowl.
Hangs back inside the crease and punches it wide of mid off for a run.
Thisara Perera has been promoted up the order as well. Sri Lanka showing pro-activeness but their batsmen not showing much fight.

OUT! Umpire's call. Sri Lanka lose their third wicket. Phehlukwayo switches to 'round the wicket for the left-hander and delivers a length ball around off. It shapes back sharply into the batsman, Perera is beaten for pace as he tries to work it around and is rapped on the pads. The bowler appeals vociferously, the umpire waits for him to complete his appeal and then quietly raises his finger. Perera consults his partner and then takes the referral. The replays roll in and they find it to be clipping the leg stump. Sri Lanka are going at a good run rate but are losing wickets at regular intervals.
Huge shout for an lbw, up goes the finger. The Kusals get together and then refer it.
FOUR! Andile digs in a short ball wide outside off, Perera stands tall and packs a punch over covers for a cracking boundary.

DROPPED! Shamsi is clumsy! Mendis gets a life. He tries heaving a length ball over mid-wicket but ends up skying it high up in the air towards long on. Shamsi moves back from mid on and then gets across a bit before diving to his left. It comes into his hands but then pops out. Should take those at this level. A single taken.
Turns it off his pads on the leg side and crosses.
Back of a length ball around off, angling away, Perera mistimes his pull shot. Almost drags it through mid-wicket and gets a couple.
Andile Phehlukwayo is the first bowling change.
Mendis lets the ball go outside his off stump.

FOUR! Not quite from the middle but enough connection to take it over the infield. A length ball angling in, Mendis lofts it over mid off, his bat turns a bit in his hand but it still goes over the fielder. A boundary results.

Are my eyes deceiving me? The playing field has gone a bit dark. Somewhere from the hills, I feel rain clouds are approaching. Thunderstorms were predicted for the afternoon today. The Lankans might just have that DLS sheet ready...
Short ball on middle, nicely pulled all along the carpet through square leg for a single.
A length ball on middle, worked on the leg side but straight to the fielder.

FOUR! This one is intentional, nearly took out his partner at the other end, Perera. Slaps a shortish ball right from where it came. Mendis falls over while trying to evade it and the ball screams through. Duminy again with the chase, reaches the ball, tries to pull it back but it brushes his hands and goes over the line.

FOUR! Surely not where he intended. A slower delivery, on a shorter length outside off, Perera tries to smash it through the line but it comes off from the inner half of the blade and hurries down the ground. Duminy gives it a chase from mid off, tries to put in a slide but his knee gets stuck on the turf. It crosses the rope and South Africa will hope JP has not done any damage to himself.
Short and on middle, pulled down to fine leg for a single.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Angling into the batsman and straightening a bit to open up Mendis. He tries defending but it takes the outside edge and speeds down to third man for a single.
Back of a length delivery on middle, Mendis rises on his back foot and taps it on the leg side. Comes out of the crease and then shouts no as Rabada quickly gets to the ball.
Movement in the air, quite visible. It curls back into the batsman from a length outside off, Mendis keeps it out off his pads to square leg.
Bouncer by Rabada, Mendis ducks underneath it.

Nearly deceives the batsman, Ngidi. Hurls in a slower length ball around middle and off, Perera without reading the variation attempts for a lofted shot. Mistimes it in the air and goes just over Duminy at mid off. Two taken.
Edgy way to get off the mark! Back f a length delivery wide outside off, Kusal throws his bat at it and edges it wide of the second slip fielder for a single.
Angles in a length ball on off, Kusal offers a straight bat in defense. The replays show that Ngidi is landing in the danger area. The umpire will be keeping a close eye on that.
Kusal Mendis walks in next with Sri Lanka in an early spot of bother. Two slips in place.

OUT! Gone! Ngidi has two. A lethal short delivery, well-directed at the batsman, Tharanga opts to play the pull shot but is in no position to do so. Ends up mistiming his shot terribly and Mulder in front of square leg makes no mistake while catching the ball. The bounce there got big on him and the pace also hurried Upul. Fine bowling by Lungi, he is growing in stature with every game.
Short in length and around off, Tharanga drags his pull shot over mid-wicket for another brace.

Another leading edge. This time off Tharanga's bat. It flies towards covers as Duminy from inside the ring stretches his right hand out to attempt for the catch. Fails to do that and they take a couple.

Another sharp delivery by Kagiso, in line of the stumps and Perera tries to flick but closes the face of the bat early. It finds the leading edge and rolls past the diving cover fielder for a couple of runs.
Wicket-to-wicket line, sharp pace, no room, Perera blocks it from the crease.
Gets behind the line of the delivery and pushes it towards mid off.
This one is angled away from the batsman, Tharanga runs it down to third man and crosses.

FOUR! Excellent shot! Sri Lanka need more of these. They cannot afford to lag behind right at the start. A touch short in length ball around middle, Upul picks it up and lofts it over mid on for a boundary.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. One run added to the total.
A length ball on middle, helped in the gap on the leg side for a run. 12 runs but a wicket from the over.

FOUR! That's some way to announce your arrival. Fetches the length ball in his half and pumps it over mid on. It seems to have gone all the way but the umpire checks it upstairs and finds that it has just bounced.
Kusal Perera gets a promotion. Walks in to bat at number 3. Fair call to replace a big-hitter with another.

OUT! Dickwella has fallen into the trap! He has this habit to play his drives aerially. South Africa have studied that flaw and hence Faf du Plessis placed himself at short cover. Ngidi bowls to the plan. Lands it full outside off and angling away, Dickwella spots the width to play the drive but fails to keep it down. The South African skipper makes no mistake as he completes the catch by going down. Niroshan is distraught. 344 needed off 278 balls for Sri Lanka. Tall ask.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Some issue with spectators moving in the balcony right over the sight-screen. All sorted in quick time though as we continue...

SIX! That has gone all the way. Tremendous connection made by Upul Tharanga. As soon as he receives the full ball in his half, he plants his front leg forward and just goes through with his lofted shot. Great timing and it clears long off. This shot will give some confidence to Tharanga. 50th biggie of his ODI career, 9th Sri Lankan to do so.
Slapped straight to point. Plenty of width on offer outside off, Tharanga hits it firmly through the line but finds the fielder.
Sharp bouncer, around leg, a late call probably by Niroshan to play the hook shot. Fails to make any connection. Quinton uses every bit of his height to collect the ball.
Fuller and outside off, driven wide of mid off for a run.
No room to work with. On a length around middle, Upul defends it back from the crease.
Width on offer outside off, it's run down wide of backward point towards third man for a single.
A leg slip in place.

Good length ball in line of the stumps, Upul taps it down towards mid-wicket and immediately calls his partner through for a run. Rabada rushes across to his left, gets to the ball, picks it up and then has a shy at the striker's end. Misses. Should have gone towards his end as Upul looked to be in danger.
Shortish and outside off, cut straight to point.

FOUR! Another boundary but it also had a hint of risk in it. Shortish in length and shaping away from the batsman, Dickwella moves back to make some space and flashes his bat through the line. It flies past the diving cover-point fielder for a boundary.
Mishit! A half-volley around off, Dickwella tries to play the cover drive but it takes the inner half of his blade and rolls to mid on.

FOUR! A bit uppish but through the gap. A length ball angling away from the batsman yet again, this time Niroshan takes his front leg forward and drives it through covers. Looked a bit loose first up but it was timed and placed quite decently.
A length ball angling away from the batsman, Dickwella stays back and plays it down towards point.
Gets behind the line of the delivery and defends it on the leg side.
A hint of movement for Ngidi and there is extra bounce as well. It's on a length around leg, Dickwella fails to keep it out and is hit on the thigh pad.
Lungi Ngidi to bowl with the second new ball.
Clocks 140.7 kph and releases a length delivery in the channel outside off, Tharanga lets it be. Top first over by Kagiso.
This one is wide outside off, an easy leave this time for Upul.

Wow, what a delivery! An inswinger landing on a good length around off. Tharanga trusts the bounce there and offers no shot. However, it shapes back in, clips the flap of his back pad and goes over the stumps. They appeal for an lbw but the umpire remains unmoved. Rabada then turns and signals to his skipper that it's too high. Good call.

Almost chops it on first ball! Rabada steams in and hurls across a lethal short ball outside off, Dickwella pushes at it well away from his body and gets an inside edge. It goes closely past the stumps to fine leg for a single.
Off the mark. A touch short again and around leg, Tharanga works it off his pads to square leg and picks up a single. Sri Lanka are away.
Starts with a back of a length ball on off, angling across the left-hander, Tharanga watches the line closely and shoulders arms.

Time for the run chase. The South African players are in a customary huddle. In-form Niroshan Dickwella and misfiring Upul Tharanga walk out to the centre to open the batting for Sri Lanka. Kagiso Rabada to begin proceedings with the first new ball. Two slips in place. Let's begin.
